Three-step regression of class membership on covariates (Mplus R3STEP)

r3step.Rd

Multinomial logistic regression of latent class membership on covariates by the bias-adjusted three-step ML method of Vermunt (2010), as Mplus AUXILIARY = x (R3STEP) (Asparouhov & Muthén 2014). The measurement model of object is kept fixed, so the covariates cannot change the classes.

Usage

r3step(
  object,
  data,
  covariates,
  ref = NULL,
  se = "robust",
  wave = NULL,
  between_covariates = NULL
)

Arguments

object

A fitted latentmix model without covariates (K >= 2).

data

Data frame with one row per row of the data the model was fitted to (same order), usually that same data frame. For backward compatibility it may also be the covariates themselves (a numeric data frame or matrix), with covariates omitted.

covariates

Covariate columns of data (tidyselect), e.g. c(x1, x2).

ref

Reference class (default: the last class).

se

"robust" (sandwich standard errors, Mplus MLR; default) or "ml" (inverse information).

wave

For an LTA: the wave whose class is regressed on the covariates (manual R3STEP with that wave's most likely class and classification errors; cases without observed indicators at that wave are left out).

between_covariates

Two-level models only: cluster-level covariates of the between class (cb ON z).

Value

An object of class c("latentmix_r3step", "latentmix_aux"), a list with

table

data frame with class, term, estimate (multinomial logit against the reference class), se, z, p, oddsratio;

n, ndeleted

rows used and rows deleted for missing covariates;

ref

the reference class;

se_type

the se argument;

text

Julia's printed summary.

Details

The most likely class is used as a single indicator of the latent class with misclassification probabilities fixed at those of the measurement model (classification_table(object)$errors), and the class is regressed on the covariates. Covariates must be numeric (dummy-code factors, e.g. with stats::model.matrix()). data must have one row per row of the data the model was fitted to, in the same order; rows with a missing covariate are deleted listwise (as in Mplus), and the number deleted is reported. For a joint (one-step) latent class regression use the covariates argument of lca() or lpa().

Sampling weights and a complex survey design (cluster, strata) of object are reused: the step-3 likelihood is weighted and robust standard errors are design-based, as Mplus R3STEP with TYPE = MIXTURE COMPLEX.

For a two-level model (lca() / lpa() with level2 and KB), r3step() is the bias-adjusted three-step estimator of Lyrvall, Bakk, Oser and Di Mari (2024): every individual gets its modal within class (posterior given its whole cluster), which enters the two-level structural model (cw ON cb, cw ON x, cb ON z) as a single indicator with fixed classification errors (Vermunt 2010). It returns a two-level model like twostep() (standard errors treat the errors as known, as Mplus does); ref, se and wave do not apply.

References

Vermunt, J. K. (2010). Latent class modeling with covariates: Two improved three-step approaches. Political Analysis, 18(4), 450–469. doi:10.1093/pan/mpq025

Asparouhov, T., & Muthén, B. (2014). Auxiliary variables in mixture modeling: Three-step approaches using Mplus. Structural Equation Modeling, 21(3), 329–341. doi:10.1080/10705511.2014.915181

See also

bch(), dcat(), coeftable() for the one-step regression, lm_table().

Examples

data(aces)
# \donttest{
# Do sex, age and parental education predict the ACE class? (three-step R3STEP)
m <- lca(aces, starts_with("ace_"), K = 4)     # 4 ACE classes, as generated
#> Starting Julia ...
r <- r3step(m, aces, c(female, age, low_parent_edu), ref = 1)
r   # log-odds of each class against class 1 (Low adversity, the largest class)
#> ━━ R3STEP: latent class regression (three-step) ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
#>   n = 1500; reference class 1; robust standard errors
#> 
#>   ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
#>   Term                  Logit     SE     OR       p
#>   ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
#>   Class 2 vs. 1
#>     (Intercept)       -0.584*  0.287  0.558   0.042
#>     female              0.155  0.175  1.168   0.376
#>     age             -0.023***  0.007  0.978  <0.001
#>     low_parent_edu   0.679***  0.176  1.972  <0.001
#>   Class 3 vs. 1
#>     (Intercept)     -1.594***  0.355  0.203  <0.001
#>     female             -0.175  0.209  0.839   0.401
#>     age                -0.002  0.007  0.998   0.835
#>     low_parent_edu   0.957***  0.211  2.603  <0.001
#>   Class 4 vs. 1
#>     (Intercept)     -1.787***  0.362  0.168  <0.001
#>     female              0.032  0.216  1.033   0.881
#>     age                -0.008  0.008  0.992   0.333
#>     low_parent_edu   0.767***  0.221  2.153  <0.001
#>   ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
#>   * p < 0.05; ** p < 0.01; *** p < 0.001
# low_parent_edu has positive log-odds for every adversity class (generated: +0.5 to +1.0)
lm_table(r, format = "markdown")
#> **Three-step (R3STEP) latent class regression**
